batch_strategy: Condition-response repair with matched loading contrasts, targeted structural transfer, and one compact nonpolar calibration control.

choices.reason: m146 at 10/1 and 100 uL is a direct loading contrast to the measured 10/1, 150 uL point 23ef03f3e75e40b20095, which reached 51.3/108.5 mL. It tests whether the late transition moves mainly in onset or also in finish.

m146 at 0/1 supplies the missing low-strength anchor below measured 2/1, 5/1, and 10/1 points 2745c6978a8911fc3dda, 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e, and 23ef03f3e75e40b20095. The label can locate where this scaffold begins its sharp solvent response.

m146 at 1/1 fills the low-to-intermediate part of the same molecule's response curve. Together with 2745c6978a8911fc3dda and 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e, it tests whether the rise toward the measured 10/1 late regime is gradual or threshold-like.
m146 at 2/1 and 150 uL is paired with measured 2/1, 100 uL record 2745c6978a8911fc3dda. It isolates a loading effect near the onset of the solvent transition while retaining the scaffold and ratio.

m206 at 0/1 provides a low-strength anchor for the fused benzyl-alcohol scaffold after the measured 5/1 and 10/1 late points 614873124b33029a924c and b7cf293311f83700cd9a. It distinguishes a delayed threshold from a broad late offset.

m206 at 2/1 samples the rising part of the curve below measured 5/1 and 10/1 records 614873124b33029a924c and b7cf293311f83700cd9a. This is useful for learning the location and curvature of the scaffold-specific transition.

m206 at 5/1 and 150 uL is a loading contrast to measured 5/1, 100 uL record 614873124b33029a924c, while the 10/1 point b7cf293311f83700cd9a anchors the stronger-eluent tail. It separates loading movement from solvent-response growth.

m11 at 2/1 and 100 uL pairs with measured 2/1, 50 uL record 3e41bb94c582476b5b6a. It extends the oxime loading curve below the sharp changes seen at 20/1 and 50/1, including 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f and efd84dffe823b6298db6.

m11 at 5/1 and 50 uL is a matched loading contrast to measured 5/1, 100 uL record 1182373ab8814dbe2f43. It tests whether the onset and compact finish remain decoupled before the high-ratio transition.

m11 at 10/1 and 50 uL contrasts with measured 10/1, 100 uL record 6b5982c6e1bbaadd6a95 and connects to the 50/1 loading pair 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f and efd84dffe823b6298db6. This tests loading sensitivity close to the developing late regime.

m11 at 0/1 supplies an early control for the oxime curve. It helps prevent the large-ratio corrections learned from 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f and efd84dffe823b6298db6 from being transferred to the compact low-strength region.

m178 at 5/1 samples below the measured 20/1 and 50/1 records 855456da9ea892f7216b and 0c5c35afb3a24375c153. It tests whether the late rise begins gradually or remains suppressed until a higher solvent ratio.

m178 at 10/1 is the missing intermediate point between measured 20/1 and 50/1 records 855456da9ea892f7216b and 0c5c35afb3a24375c153. Its label can discriminate the previously predicted plateau from a continuing transition.

m28 at 2/1 fills the multifunctional-carbonyl response between measured 1/1 record 0d18f3f10c8377d12316, 5/1 record bfbe491a54086b98874d, and 10/1 record 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a. It is a useful interpolation point for a steep condition curve.

m28 at 5/1 and 150 uL is a loading contrast to measured 5/1, 100 uL record bfbe491a54086b98874d and can be compared with the 10/1 loading pair 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a and 0dccaa29989ef4956786. It tests whether loading changes onset more than finish.

m90 at 5/1 and 150 uL probes the pyridyl ester family after the large underprediction at measured 10/1, 100 uL record 96710afeabc594baa359. The wide predicted interval makes this a high-impact test of basic-ring and carbonyl-context transfer.

m90 at 2/1 and 150 uL locates the lower-ratio part of the pyridyl ester response below 96710afeabc594baa359. It can show whether the large late behavior emerges smoothly or through a scaffold-specific threshold.

m90 at 0/1 supplies an early anchor for the same low-similarity pyridyl ester. Together with the measured failure 96710afeabc594baa359, it constrains both graph-context transfer and the shape of the solvent response.

m66 at 2/1 tests a carbonyl-substituted pyridine below the measured 5/1 failure 49201b5817f204116f7f, whose finish was underestimated by nearly 95 mL. This label can determine whether the failure starts at moderate solvent strength or only at the stronger point.

m205 at 2/1 provides a lower-ratio transfer point for the naphthylethanol scaffold after measured 5/1 record 48853fd78c77153b963a showed a large underprediction. It tests how linker and ring context affect the onset of delayed alcohol retention.

m205 at 5/1 and 50 uL is a loading contrast to measured 5/1, 100 uL record 48853fd78c77153b963a. It tests whether the broad late interval is intrinsic to the scaffold or partly loading-dependent, while also informing transfer from m206.

m86 at 5/1 and 50 uL complements measured 2/1, 50 uL record d7f5057912ffbf1231a3 and 5/1, 100 uL record 3ccd6444c8a55917fbf8. The point tests positional amino-ester response and loading sensitivity in a family where onset and finish were both underpredicted.

m88 at 2/1 and 50 uL probes the low-ratio side of the amino-ester family after the large measured 5/1 error at d2921349ba8d9cef15a4. It discriminates a positional graph effect from a general amino-ester retention correction.

m88 at 1/1 and 100 uL adds a second low-to-intermediate anchor around the measured 5/1 failure d2921349ba8d9cef15a4. The paired points can teach whether the unusual finish is already present before the stronger mobile phase.

m141 at 10/1 and 50 uL is a high-width test of a compact methylpyridine graph environment at strong solvent. It extends the basic-aromatic transfer problem represented by measured pyridyl failures 49201b5817f204116f7f and 96710afeabc594baa359.

m202 at 10/1 and 150 uL has a large model quantile width and probes a phosphorus-containing donor/acceptor environment in a late predicted regime. Its label can reveal whether the current feature representation transfers across heteroatom arrangements rather than simply across polarity totals.

m129 at 20/1 and 100 uL tests a strong-eluent continuation for the thioether aldehyde family. The measured 50/1 m129 record d54c93a11164b4abac6e was already late, so this point can distinguish a plateau from further growth and inform related oxygenated carbonyl rows.

m129 at 5/1 supplies the lower-ratio anchor needed to interpret the measured 50/1 behavior at d54c93a11164b4abac6e. It tests whether this sulfur-containing aldehyde develops late retention earlier than the model predicts.

m195 at 50/1 and 150 uL is a high-width fused aromatic aldehyde experiment in a region where strong-eluent tails are sparsely constrained. It tests late graph transfer without assuming that the m146 or m178 correction applies to all fused aromatics.

m119 at 5/1 and 150 uL is a loading contrast to measured 5/1, 100 uL record 776ee2c1e85ebde75168, which showed a large underprediction. It directly tests whether the ether-substituted alcohol's broad interval changes mainly in onset or in finish.

m72 at 20/1 with PE mobile phase and 50 uL samples a high-width condition region adjacent to the measured DCM 20/1 point 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327. The solvent-system change tests transfer across recorded conditions while retaining a strongly polar amino-ester scaffold.

m9 at 20/1 with PE provides a compact nonpolar calibration row. It tests whether late-retention corrections spread into ordinary aromatic rows, complementing the measured compact heavy-halogen control f81578588e5df2eb7e54.

hypotheses.content: Late solvent-response transitions are scaffold-specific and can occur abruptly between intermediate and strong mobile phases. Recent m11, m146, m206, and m178 outcomes support this, while lower-ratio portions of several curves remain under-sampled.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched curve points can teach the predictor where transitions begin, how sharply both endpoints move, and which scaffold corrections should remain local rather than being generalized across the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected low and intermediate points locate the transitions for m146, m206, m11, m178, m28, m90, and m129, or do some of these curves remain compact until a stronger threshold?

hypotheses.content: In several measured families, increased loading advances V1 more than it changes V2, but the direction and size of this effect are scaffold-dependent. The m211 loading behavior remains a counterexample that prevents a universal rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The current predictor often gives nearly invariant loading responses. Matched loading pairs can improve both endpoint targets while teaching the model when loading effects are asymmetric or reverse direction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m146, m206, m11, m28, m205, and m119 loading contrasts reproduce onset-dominant shifts, or do some scaffolds show finish-dominant or nonmonotonic loading behavior?

hypotheses.content: Graph context and functional-group surroundings affect retention and solvent sensitivity beyond coarse donor, acceptor, polarity, or aromaticity counts. Basic-site environment, linker topology, positional substitution, and accessibility are plausible contributors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest failures include low-similarity pyridyl, amino-ester, aromatic-alcohol, and fused-ring structures. Related labels can teach graph-condition interactions that generalize beyond molecule-level offsets.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural distinctions transfer across pyridyl carbonyls, amino esters, fused alcohols, sulfur aldehydes, and other heteroatom-rich aromatic scaffolds after their loading conditions are accounted for?

hypotheses.content: Broad finishes under EA-rich or strong-eluent conditions are scaffold-specific; the predictor's broad-tail extrapolation should be downweighted without matched labels. Compact m117 and m164 outcomes weaken any universal broad-tail rule while broad acid behavior shows that broad intervals remain chemically possible.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Separating genuine scaffold-specific tails from model-generated broad intervals prevents corrections learned from a few extreme rows from degrading common EA-rich and compact rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which high-width candidates retain broad finishes after measurement, and which collapse to compact intervals like the measured m117 and m164 cases?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strongly support scaffold-specific solvent transitions: m11 changed sharply across 5/1, 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1; m146 rose from the 2/1 and 5/1 points into the late 10/1 regime; m206 showed the same late response; and m178 at 50/1 rejected the earlier plateau prediction. The batch therefore emphasizes low and intermediate curve points rather than another isolated extreme. The m11 loading pair, together with m204 and m107, supports an onset-dominant loading effect, but the m211 observations remain contradictory, so matched loading experiments remain useful. Large failures for m66, m90, m205, m86, m88, and m119 strengthen the case for graph-condition transfer experiments. The m117 and m164 results weaken universal broad-tail extrapolation: broad intervals remain possible, as in m173, but are not implied by EA-rich or strong-eluent conditions alone.
batch_rationale: The batch contains several interpretable local response curves: m146 and m206 cover lower-to-late solvent strength, m11 adds multiple loading contrasts, m178 samples the region below its newly observed late point, m28 and m90 constrain steep polar and pyridyl responses, and m129 adds a sulfur-containing aldehyde curve. Loading contrasts are distributed across m146, m206, m11, m28, m205, and m119 so the retrained model can learn whether endpoint movement is asymmetric rather than receiving a single scaffold-specific example. The m66, m86, m88, m141, m202, m195, and m72 rows target structural transfer and high-width regions exposed by prior failures, with m205 and m119 linking those tests to measured alcohol-family errors. The m9 row provides a compact nonpolar calibration point to limit overcorrection of ordinary rows. Together these labels repair high-consequence tails, identify where the model's chemistry representation fails, and provide local anchors that can generalize across the heterogeneous Row-distribution.
